name: Martinswand
kurzbeschreibung: The nearly 700 m high Martinswand near Zirl: Emperor Maximilian legend, Maximiliansgrotte cave, and world-famous via ferratas above the Inn Valley.
beschreibung:
Overview

The imposing Martinswand is a nearly 700-metre-high, sheer vertical limestone cliff on the southern edge of the Karwendel range in the Tyrolean Inn Valley, approximately ten kilometres west of Innsbruck. Located in the municipality of Zirl, the massive rock bastion drops dramatically right beside the A12 Inntal autobahn and the Inn River bed. As a historic site, the backdrop of one of Tyrol's most famous imperial legends, and an internationally celebrated rock-climbing hub, this cliff has captivated travellers for centuries.

The Legend of Emperor Maximilian I & Climbing

The Martinswand achieved legendary fame through the tale of Emperor Maximilian I: in the spring of 1494, while hunting chamois on the brittle cliffs, the passionate imperial huntsman reportedly climbed into an impasse from which he could neither advance nor retreat. For two agonizing days, the young monarch clung to a narrow rocky ledge fearing for his life while the valley below prayed for his rescue. According to legend, a young shepherd boy (believed by locals to be a guardian angel named Oswald Zips) appeared and guided him safely through hidden rock terraces back down to the valley. In eternal gratitude, Maximilian commissioned the construction of the Maximiliansgrotte in a natural cave halfway up the wall, marking it with a colossal, far-visible wooden cross and statues of saints. Today, the cliff is a climbing mecca: the demanding Kaiser-Max-Klettersteig (upper section graded E) is considered one of the steepest and most challenging sport via ferratas in the Eastern Alps. At the base of the wall, climbing gardens offer over 200 bolted routes of all grades.

Visit & Arrival

The Martinswand, the grotto trail, and the via ferratas are freely accessible free of charge during the snow-free season from March to November (beware of rockfall hazards in winter or wet conditions!). A historic, rock-hewn path leads up to the Maximiliansgrotte (approx. 45 minutes walking time from the Brunntal car park near Zirl). By car: Via the Inntal autobahn A12 or regional road B171 to Zirl; paid climbers' car parks are located at the eastern edge of Zirl close to the cliff. By public transport: S-Bahn Tirol (lines S4, S5) to Zirl station or VVT regional bus line 4125 to the stop Zirl Martinswand / Gh Martinsbühel.

Tips

Sturdy hiking boots and alpine surefootedness are strictly necessary for the hike to the Maximiliansgrotte (the trail is exposed in places and secured with wire ropes). Climbers tackling the Kaiser-Max-Klettersteig must carry a complete certified via ferrata set with helmet and resting sling; novices should only venture on this route accompanied by certified mountain guides.
